s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on MRI
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
MRI showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with pathology showing spindled cells and positive CD34 immunohistochemistry

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to spindle cell lipoma, with mixed fibrous and adipose tissue and variable cell morphology

shortlist.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the presence of adipose tissue and atypical cells, although less likely

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common, this tumor can present with a bruise-like lesion and has a similar immunohistochemical profile

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of adipose tissue and the potential for vascular involvement

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Simple lipoma is a possibility, although the presence of atypical cells and pigment deposition makes this less likely

shortlist.label: Gardner-Diamond syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: This rare condition involves painful bruising and could be considered, although the pathology does not fully support this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a painful bruise, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, along with strong positivity for CD34, are consistent with a Nora lesion, a rare, painful, and pigmented lipomatous lesion.

rejected.label: Spindle cell lipoma
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic floret-like cells and absence of S100 positivity

rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
rejected.why: Absence of floret-like cells and lack of S100 positivity

rejected.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
rejected.why: Lesion size and location, along with the absence of MDM2 amplification, make this less likely

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic storiform pattern and CD34 positivity without other specific markers

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Presence of extensive pigment deposition and spindled cells, which are not typical of a simple lipoma

rejected.label: Gardner-Diamond syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of personal or family history of bleeding disorders and absence of characteristic autoerythrocyte sensitization
